title: Running image as root in podman when Containerfile has defined a USER
question:
Im not sure if this is doable and if it is it would have some security issued related

I have an image with an Apache Spark installation that sets a specific USER 185 in its Containerfile. When I run it normally it runs within the image as user 185. Problem is I need to be root for one specific operation. I need to create a config file under /opt/spark/config but given that folder has only permits for root, I cannot really set any config. This causes the Spark drivers and executors run with some parameters I dont want to use, or empty parameters. I cannot pass those parameters either in the spark-submit or in the sparkContext in the pyspark script.

Given I cannot run podman as sudo podman either (I dont have root permits in my corp laptop), what can I do to run some commands as root when I run the image in podman?
answer:
1. If you can modify the image:

    • Solution: Create a new Containerfile extending the original image, change /opt/spark/config ownership to UID 185.

      • Containerfile: FROM <spark-image> \n USER root \n RUN chown -R 185:185 /opt/spark/config \n USER 185

      • Build: podman build -t custom-spark .

      • Run: podman run -it custom-spark <command>

  2. If you cannot modify the image:

    • Solution: Mount a local directory to /opt/spark/config.

      • Create dir: mkdir ~/spark-config; chmod 700 ~/spark-config

      • Run: podman run -v ~/spark-config:/opt/spark/config:Z -it <spark-image> <command>

  3. If you need runtime permission changes:

    • Solution: Use podman unshare to adjust permissions.

      • Start: podman run -d --name spark-container <spark-image> sleep infinity

      • Adjust: podman unshare chown -R 185:185 /opt/spark/config

      • Execute: podman exec spark-container <command>

      • Clean: podman stop spark-container; podman rm spark-container

  4. If you can use Spark configuration alternatives:

    • Solution: Set parameters via spark-submit or environment variables.

      • Run: podman run -it <spark-image> spark-submit --conf spark.config.option=value script.py or -e SPARK_CONFIG_OPTION=value
